items.desc: Mimi Gilbert is a proudly independent artist who’s spent the better part of the last ten years living, touring and creating music in Australia and Aotearoa, New Zealand. Raised on an orange orchard in Ojai, California and now based in Los Angeles, Mimi crafts careful folk songs with a sensitivity toward the natural world; as hopefully insightful as they are quietly devastating. At just 15-years-old they found the freedom they longed for away from a super religious household and out in the world busking on streets and at train stations along the west coast with her brother. items.title: No Skips with Mimi Gilbert

items.desc: Abbe May is Western Australia’s very own fruit-forward, fairy godmother of rock. Known for her big guitar riffs and bigger hats, she’s one of our most respected and beloved performers; a phenomenal songwriter, guitarist and mentor. Abbe spent her late teens and early twenties on the stages of some of Australia’s most notorious rock venues and festivals, playing alongside Neneh Cherry, The Black Keys, Midnight Oil, The Motels, Art vs. Science, Tim Rogers, Adalita and so many more! items.title: No Skips with Abbe May

items.desc: Over the last two decades, Welsh musician and producer Cate Le Bon has built a catalogue of soft-worn post-punk and abstract art-pop, and a sound entirely her own. She’s also played a role in shaping the work of some truly beloved indie acts over the last decade, from Dry Cleaning to Kurt Vile, Wilco, St Vincent and Horsegirl. In this conversation with Pam Boland, recorded in April of 2026 following the release of her album Michelangelo Dying, Cate share the songs that have most influenced her creatively, her love of physical media and the making of her latest album.
